characterList.description: A young man with short dark hair, wearing a black New York Yankees hooded sweatshirt and a black Yankees cap. He has eye black under his eyes.
characterList.name: Aaron Judge

content_metadata.description: Post-game interview with Aaron Judge discussing his performance, challenges, and experiences during the game.

qAndA.answer: Although he says he had a good feeling off the bat, he didn’t know where it would land. He felt a sense of relief once he saw it land in the fan's glove.
qAndA.question: What was Judge's reaction immediately after hitting the home run?

qAndA.answer: Judge consciously chose to focus on the team's success and the 'daily grind' rather than dwelling on the pressure of the record. This mindset helped him stay grounded and perform at his best.
qAndA.question: How did Judge's approach to the pressure of the home run chase affect his performance?

qAndA.answer: Judge said he was thinking of his wife, his family, his teammates, and the fans who had supported him throughout the season.
qAndA.question: What specific details did Judge share about his emotional state while rounding the bases after hitting the home run?

qAndA.answer: Judge's acceptance of the situation and his acknowledgment of the fan's right to keep the ball demonstrate his humility and his focus on team success over personal gain.
qAndA.question: What does Judge's reaction to not getting the home run ball back reveal about his character?

qAndA.answer: Judge expects the true weight of his accomplishment to sink in after the season concludes, suggesting he is currently focused on the team's post-season goals and that he will have more time for personal reflection in the off-season.
qAndA.question: How does Judge believe the significance of his accomplishment will evolve over time?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Aaron, in the first game, it looked like you were a little frustrated after the pop-up.
How did you feel after that first game and going into this game?
And also, will you play tomorrow?
Yeah, it was frustrated because I wasn't helping the team out.
I had a couple bad at bats, swinging at some bad pitches, missing my pitch.
So I was upset that as the lead off guy, I got to get on base.
I hadn't been doing that.
The Rangers, they were coming after me and they were attacking me.
I just didn't put any good swings on it.
So I was pretty upset of myself.
I was supposed to be a table-setter.
And tomorrow, I'm hoping to play.
We got one more game.
We'll see what's the kid has to say about that.
But I'm hoping to be in there.
Yeah, Aaron, what did you know about Jose Tinoco?
I know he has a nasty sinker and a nasty slider.
I know we were kind of waiting to hear who the starter of game two was going to be.
When I heard it was him, I saw what he did the night before.
I was like, I don't know if this isn't a good match up to start the game off with a guy
with high velocity like that and a good off speed pitch.
So I think going into it, I think that kind of helped me relax.
Like, hey, this is a good pitcher.
Let me just go up there and let's see what happens.
I was able to get one over the heart of the plate and try to put a good swing on it.
Just give us the early lead.
Aaron, when you look at the last couple of weeks when it really became a home run chase,
what do you think you will remember most about this experience?
The fans, the fans at home, the fans on the road, the constant support, seeing Yankee Stadium
on their feet for everything like that.
They're booing pictures for throwing balls, which I've never seen before.
I think I got to base it the other night and I was getting booed for a single.
It's just a little moment like that.
You look back on what have been great to do at Yankee Stadium in front of our home fans.
I know a lot of Yankee fans that travel well.
They travel well.
There's a lot of Yankee fans here tonight and getting a chance to share that experience
with the fans.
That's what it's about for me.
Right here.
Aaron, were you able to get the ball back?
Not yet.
I don't know where it's at.
We'll see what happens with that.
It'd be great to get it back, but it's as a souvenir for a fan.
They made a great catch out there and they got every right to it.
Aaron, at any point during this, did you feel stress, pressure that you had to get this
done?
It's tough to say because every game is stressful.
I kind of felt bad for my teammates because like I said, every single out bad, I got teammates
stacked up.
They're on top of the step waiting for me to do this.
I hit a double or I'd walk or I'd do something.
I kind of felt like I was letting them down.
Even the fans, all the fans that would pack to Yankee Stadium and the fans that came
here these past two games.
I felt like I let them down.
If I had a two-for-four game or a one-for-two game with a couple of walks, I felt like I
was letting them down.
I never tried to think about it as pressure.
I tried to enjoy every single moment and not really think about, hey, they're all on the
feet for you.
To go see you hit a home run, I tried to think about, hey, they're here to see an exciting
ball game and see something special.
Just having that mindset kind of helped me stay pretty calm.
There's definitely a little pressure in there, but you know, you just try to block
that out.
You take a couple of walks right here.
So Aaron, you talked about your family.
You talked about your teammates, but a lot of players around baseball, especially some
of the higher name players, some of the more marquee players, they're excited about
this and they tweeted out, obviously, I haven't seen that part yet, but just seeing
players around baseball talk about this and be excited for you.
What do you think about that?
It's incredible.
I think that's one of the biggest honors is any compliment from your peers.
The guys that are out there grinding just like you are on a daily basis, they know how hard
this game is, they know how hard it is to show up and post every single night so that
here or for them to tweet things out, say things like that, there's no higher honor in my
book.
That's what's always been about for me is my teammates and even my peers and the respect
I have for other players around the league to get that same respect back.
That's, it gives you chills to be honest.
Take the last three right here.
Aaron, has your number was growing higher and higher?
You kept saying numbers don't matter, I'm worried about the wins.
Was there a time maybe home or at some point you just said yourself, wow, I could do this.
Was there a moment?
Well, I think going into the every year, every season, you ride down goals, you have stuff
you want to accomplish.
So every year I think I can go out there and hit 70 homers or have the confidence in faith
to go out there and try to do something special for the team.
But when you're in the process, that's a fun part.
You don't think about that.
You're so locked in on the daily grind that the number is and all that kind of stuff.
It's just a wash.
For me, I enjoy the daily grind of working at bat and getting a base hit to help the team
or driving an RBI, the grind of having a tough day at the plate where you're over four
and things are going your way.
And I guess what I got to wake up and show up tomorrow because I got a big game here
in a couple hours.
So that for me, I just had fun getting locked in on that process.
I'll break your call.
And when you hit the ball left your bat, do you know it was gone for sure if it was
going to be high enough?
I had a good feeling off the bat.
I've been played too many games here at the New Park.
I know the old park, the ball really, the ball flew out of here.
So I knew I had a good chance at the old park.
But here, you never know, but I had a good feeling off the bat.
I just didn't know where it was going to land or what it was going to hit.
It was a good sense of relief once it, I saw it landing that fans glove and we're up
one nothing.
And now a chance to see Garrett go out there and break their other records.
So I was at a good feeling off the bat.
And we went out.
What was your, when you stole the base as far as you think and what was going through
your mind?
I just think of my wife thinking of my family.
My teammates, just the fans, all that was kind of running through my head.
Just the constant support I've gotten through this whole process through this whole year,
from them, especially.
That's all I really running through my head.
And then I was looking forward to getting the dug out and going back on defense.
So watch Garrett go out there and break a record.
So I had quite a few emotions kind of going there.
It's only been a few hours, but have you been able to fully process the historical significance
of this home run?
Oh, no, yeah.
It's in my book, It's just another day.
You know, I wish you would have got the win.
I would have made it a little sweeter for me and Garrett, I think.
But, you know, that's what we got tonight for.
You know, to kind of soak it in and soak in the moment, soak in the mobile with my family
and then get ready for the game tomorrow.
I think it really won't seek in until, you know, the offseason after the postseason,
all that kind of stuff happens because that's still our main goal and our main focus.
So I think once we get past all that and go out there and do our job, then we can kind
of soak it all in.
